# WEB-M2: frontend contracts vs the real API schema

**Pinned API:** `ui/u4-migration-readiness` @ `a9a80f7` (WEB-PREP2), exported read-only into a
temporary directory and run with `uvicorn baseball_api.app:app --port 8601` over the real Lahman
data (1871–2025).

**Schema:** `web/openapi/baseball-api.json` (OpenAPI 3.1.0, 6 paths, 29 schemas), with
`web/openapi/baseball-api.meta.json` recording the commit.

**Types:** `web/src/lib/api/generated/baseball-api.ts`, generated by `npm run api:types`
(openapi-typescript 7.13.0). `npm run api:types:check` fails if the generated file drifts from
the pinned schema, and it runs first in `npm run check`.

**How the fields are used:**
- The wire format is the generated types. The HTTP adapter (`lib/api/http/`) is the only code
  that reads it.
- Pages keep the WEB-M1 view models (`lib/api/types.ts`). Each view-model field is filled
  **directly** from an API field, or left **empty / hidden** when the API doesn't provide it
  yet.
- The adapter never ranks, filters, sums, qualifies or writes sentences.

## Schema facts that differ from WEB-M1's assumptions

| # | Real schema | WEB-M1 view model assumed | Resolution in WEB-M2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Field names are snake_case (`total_rows`, `player_id`, `split_mode`) | camelCase | The adapter maps names; no meaning changes |
| 2 | `SeasonLeadersResult.headline` only | `answer {headline, detail, context}` | `headline` is used. `detail` and `context` are **empty** until **R2**. The page shows the headline alone |
| 3 | No tile selection | `keyMetrics` | **Empty** until R2, so no metric tiles on real data |
| 4 | No `LeaderboardResult` answer | `answer {headline, detail}` | Until **R3**: no answer sentence. The page shows a data-free title ("Leaders by OPS, 2020–2025"), then the API's ranking |
| 5 | `Qualification {applies, min_ab, qualified_ab, mode, text}`. `text` is Markdown and names a Streamlit control | `{kind, summary, minAtBats}` | `kind` comes from `applies` + `mode`; `minAtBats` = `min_ab`. **`text` isn't shown** (it would tell web users to use a control that doesn't exist). The chip shows the number only ("Minimum 2,349 AB, qualified"). Full copy waits on **R4** |
| 6 | `MetricInfo {key, label, kind, decimals}` with no plain name | `name` ("home runs") | `name` falls back to the API `label` ("HR") until **R5** |
| 7 | No catalog endpoint | catalog (metrics, defaults, years) | Interim, see the next table. Year bounds come from `/health.seasons`. **R1** replaces it |
| 8 | `rows` ≤ 200, no offset, no export | full table | The table shows the returned page plus "Showing N of total_rows". Paging and export wait on **R6** |
| 9 | No `player_id` filter on `/seasons`, and rows below the minimum are dropped | the one-player view, with below-minimum rows marked | **Hidden in API mode** (client capability `playerSeasonRanking: false`) until **R8** |
| 10 | `LeaderboardRow` has no seasons count, and `stats.G` is `null` on leaderboard rows (the span aggregation doesn't total games) | `seasons` | **Empty.** Cards show no sub-line. They would show `G` if the API filled it; a seasons/games total belongs with R1/R6 |
| 11 | `LeaderboardRow.score` sits beside `stats` | `stats.score` | Copied into the stats map unchanged |
| 12 | `TeamRef {team_id, name, season_name, league}` | `team` string | `team` = `team_id` (short labels); `teamName` = `season_name ?? name` (the table, like Streamlit's historical team name) |
| 13 | `StatLine` keys `G…OPS` with `2B`/`3B` wire names; rates rounded to 3 | `StatLine` record | Used as-is |
| 14 | `min_{STAT}` is declared as one literal query parameter | — | Documented placeholder for `min_HR`, `min_OPS`, …. Not used by WEB-M2 yet |
| 15 | `SEASON_METRICS` accepts `yearID`; the Streamlit "Sort by" doesn't offer it | 13 stats | Not offered (Streamlit parity). R1 should say which metrics each page offers |
| 16 | `/health.build` reports the tree's deploy marker (`3713de5`), not the running commit | — | The pinned commit is recorded in `baseball-api.meta.json` instead |
| 17 | Requests during the ~18 s data load wait on a lock | — | The frontend shows its loading state, and the proxy allows 30 s |
| 18 | Error envelope `{error: {code, message, details?}}` | four error kinds | 422/404/409 → `invalid_request`; 503/502/504 or network → `unavailable`; 500 → `unknown`. The mock-only `unsupported` kind never occurs |

## Interim catalog (until R1)

The controls need option lists before the first answer arrives. Until `GET /catalog` exists, the
HTTP adapter uses these values. Each one is checked against the live API by
`npm run test:live`, so a change on the Python side fails a test instead of drifting silently.

| Value | Interim source | Live check |
|---|---|---|
| Year bounds | `/health.seasons` (live) | — |
| Historical Explorer stats | the Streamlit "Sort by" list (13 stats) | equals `invalid_metric.details.allowed` minus `yearID` |
| Leaderboards stats | the Streamlit "Sort by" list (14, including `score`) | equals `invalid_metric.details.allowed` |
| Defaults (2010–last HR desc; 2020–last score) | the documented API defaults | equal to what `/seasons` and `/leaderboards` echo when no parameters are sent |
| Display format per stat (rate vs count) | the `StatLine` rate keys (BA, OBP, SLG, OPS) | equal to `MetricInfo.kind` for each stat |

## What real data shows today (a9a80f7)

**Historical Explorer:**
- the API headline;
- the qualification chip (numbers only);
- the top-10 ranking bars;
- next steps;
- the ranked table (the first page of up to 25 rows).

Missing until the API adds them: the detail sentence, context line and metric tiles (R2).

**Leaderboards:**
- a data-free title;
- the qualification chip;
- the top 3 cards;
- the top-10 bars;
- next steps;
- the full ranking (first page);
- the weights.

Missing until the API adds them: the answer sentence and score sentence (R3).

**Hidden:** the "One player" view (R8).

## Verification (WEB-M2 integration slice)

Run against the exported API at `a9a80f7` over the real Lahman data. Nothing in the u4 worktree
or branch was touched: the export was made by `git archive` into a temporary directory and run
with bytecode writing off.

- **`npm run check`:** passes. It runs `api:types:check` (no drift), typecheck, lint, 100
  unit/component tests in 15 files and the production build.
- **`npm run test:live`:** 8 live tests pass:
  - the schema paths match the pin;
  - the interim stat lists, defaults, labels and formats equal the live API;
  - the Historical Explorer and leaderboard mappings equal the direct API responses;
  - live errors map correctly;
  - player search works.
- **Production safety:**
  - `next build` with `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASEBALL_DATA_SOURCE=mock` exits 1;
  - a normal production build contains no fixture content, source maps included;
  - the browser never calls the Python origin directly: every request goes through
    `/api/baseball/*`.
- **Browser (Chromium, production build + proxy + real API), 23 checks pass:**
  - widths 1280 / 430 / 390 / 360 on both pages, for HR/score and OPS;
  - API headlines and values equal the API responses;
  - no sample badge;
  - no one-player control, and a one-player deep link gets the honest state with no request
    sent;
  - stat change and Back on a 360 px phone;
  - an outage shows the error state, and Retry recovers;
  - an unknown stat is caught;
  - an arbitrary range (1990–2000) is answered from real data;
  - no horizontal overflow; the answer starts at about 274 px on phones;
  - axe-core: 0 violations in light and dark.

## Real data vs the WEB-M1 samples

The sample numbers were placeholders, and the real API differs, as expected:

| Example | WEB-M1 sample | Real API |
|---|---|---|
| Historical Explorer total (2010–2025, HR) | 9,718 seasons | 24,261 |
| Qualified hitters, OPS 2020–2025 | 142 | 79 |
| Judge OPS 2020–2025 | 1.058 | 1.068 |
| Name spelling | "José Ramírez" | "Jose Ramirez" (Lahman) |

None of the sample values can reach a production build.
